# Research decisions and benchmark evidence

Start with [current documentation](../README.md), not historical reports. These studies record decisions at their pinned revisions; they do not change SPEC, public API contracts or ADR status. Current gate commands and baseline selection live in [workflow](../agents/workflow.md).

## Retention and reproduction

- Frozen `baseline-v*` and `typescript-v*` directories remain intact, including apparently duplicate results. Their READMEs are versioned protocols/amendments, not disposable narrative. Begin with [Python v1](baseline-v1/README.md), [TypeScript v1](typescript-v1/README.md) and [TypeScript corpus amendment](typescript-v2/README.md); follow the workflow for the current comparison target.
- Research READMEs summarize decisions, decisive measurements, corrections, negative results and limits. Keep their preregistrations, task/corpus manifests, scripts, inputs and raw results together: studies import other studies' scripts. Do not flatten directories or regenerate frozen controls to fix a failure.
- Follow each report's pinned source revision, corpus/split, dependency versions and reproduction commands. Historical harnesses may need retired code or paid/credentialed providers; their results are not measurements of the current checkout.
- Some provider traces, corpora and raw timing logs were external even before consolidation. Committed summaries/results alone do not make those experiments independently reproducible. Reports disclose the missing inputs; do not promote such evidence beyond its limits.
- Full pre-consolidation reports, including detailed commands and interpretation, remain at [this immutable evidence tree](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/phase-6). For any shortened report, use the same relative path there. Evidence standards: [review policy](../review/evidence-and-benchmarks.md).

## Decision map

| Question | Reports |
|---|---|
| Graph ranking, dispatch and candidate-pool ceilings | [v1](graph-v1/README.md), [v2](graph-v2/README.md), [v3](graph-v3/README.md) |
| Graph navigation completeness and targeted resolution | [initial audit](graph-navigation/README.md), [correction and follow-up](graph-navigation-v2/README.md), [NetworkX projection](networkx-v1/README.md) |
| Agent-guided context and where to stop | [AGC](agc/README.md), [v2](agc-v2/README.md), [v3](agc-v3/README.md), [v4](agc-v4/README.md) |
| Optional judges and deterministic decision boundary | [seam](decision-seam/README.md), [study v1](decision-study-v1/README.md), [v2](decision-study-v2/README.md), [v3](decision-study-v3/README.md), [reliability](jev-reliability/README.md) |
| Historical JEV ordering milestones | [M1](jev-order-m1/README.md), [M2](jev-order-m2/README.md), [M3 release readiness](jev-order-m3/README.md), [release blockers](release-blockers/README.md) |
| Storage, graph caches and FTS footprint | [LEANN/storage](leann-graph-storage/README.md), [FTS corrections and optimizations](fts-footprint/README.md) |
| Output serialization | [TOON rejection](toon-serialization/README.md) |
| Retrieval diagnostics | [source bodies](source-body-retrieval/README.md), [entry retrieval](entry-retrieval-diagnostic/README.md), [file localization](file-localization/README.md), [path hints](path-hint-utility/README.md), [reachability](router-reachability/README.md), [routed selection](routed-module-selection/README.md) |

| Capture/indexing performance | [throughput](indexing-throughput/README.md), [incremental indexing](incremental-indexing/README.md), [change classification](change-classification/README.md) |

## Language milestone evidence

[JavaScript](javascript-v1/README.md), [Rust](rust-v1/README.md), [Go](go-v1/README.md), [Java](java-v1/README.md), [C](c-v1/README.md), [C++](cpp-v1/README.md). TypeScript evidence is the versioned protocol series above. Current support boundaries are documented under [parser limits](../parser-limits.md), not inferred from an old milestone's claims.

# OXIDE development workflow

Commands and verification for OXIDE v2, loaded on demand from the root
`AGENTS.md` routing table. Older docs and code comments that cite
"`AGENTS.md`" for a command or harness detail mean this file.

## Commands

[Mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html) is the one entrypoint;
`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).

```bash
mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/
mise run test          #   pytest (tests/python/)
```

`uv run pyrefly check` is an optional second type checker (`[tool.pyrefly]` in
`pyproject.toml`). It is not part of `verify` or CI; mypy `--strict` stays the gate.
On 2026-10-31 it reported 32 errors.

Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/`.
`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
frozen `docs/phase-6/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); v1's README is the
protocol (splits, gate rules, how to freeze a new version) and each later README states
its amendments. Gold is audited (`gold-audit.json`); only verified gold is gated.
Develop on the dev split; never tune on held-out.
`tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` is the same ruler for TypeScript (protocol in
`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, corpora amendment in `typescript-v2/`, latest frozen
baseline `typescript-v15/`; corpora in `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench-ts/corpora-v2/`, and the
sources-only `corpora/` only reproduces v1). Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate
needs ~2 GB of corpora and ~15 minutes, so it is `mise run contextbench-ts`, not part of
`verify`. Run it under the limits below before and after any TypeScript retrieval,
resolution, routing or packing change.
Dependencies live in `pyproject.toml` with a committed `uv.lock`; add them
with `uv add`, never by hand-editing the lock. Keep heavy local runs within
`CPUQuota=200%`/`MemoryMax=3G` (`systemd-run --user --scope`).
To verify another supported Python, set `UV_PYTHON` and a separate
`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` for the entire check. `uv sync --python` alone does not
carry that interpreter choice into a later `uv run`.

OXIDE's engine, CLI, MCP server and distribution need no Node.js, Bun or Rust
toolchain. Native Python dependencies are installed as wheels; the Platforms
workflow enforces wheel-only third-party installation and runs the installed
smoke with only the environment's scripts on `PATH`. That smoke also checks
that MCP advertises exactly `oxide_search`. Optional agent tooling (CodeGraph,
Context7, archify, external MCP servers) and GitHub Actions have their own runtimes;
they are not OXIDE dependencies. See the
[legacy infrastructure audit](../migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) for
the inventory and process ancestry.

Tests never write to real user data: `tests/python/conftest.py` gives every
test a private `OXIDE_DATA_DIR` and XDG locations, fails the session if the
real data location changes, and every subprocess receives explicit private
locations (`env()` and `python()` there; `env()` refuses any location outside
the temporary root). Native probes that could crash, and crash injection, run
only in such subprocesses. Lexical tests need the pinned FTS extension
(`uv run oxide prepare`, once), and the context-quality gate the corpora
(`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py fetch`, once; both are in bootstrap).

## Commits

Commit only when asked. OXIDE v2 work commits on `rewrite/v2` (or a branch
from it, merged back by PR); never commit v2 work to `main`, which keeps the
legacy v1 implementation until the rewrite is merged by explicit decision. Messages use a
lowercase prefix plus an imperative summary: `fix:`, `feat:`, `refactor:`,
`docs:`, `harden:`, `bench:`, `tierb:`.

## Historical reproduction

Retained `eval-agent/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`, `scripts/perf.sh` and Rust
regression/conformance fixtures are historical evidence, not current build steps.
Use the matching pinned tree (`ac985b28` for v1, `f79808a` for the replaced
Rust/Bun v2 runtime), its manifests and original report commands. The legacy
ContextBench evaluator requires Python 3.11; old TS/TSX task verification uses Bun.
See the [infrastructure decision summary](../migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md)
for the retention boundary and pinned original audit. Do not apply v1 CLI,
embedding or SQLite contracts to the Python engine.

## LadybugDB FTS extension

LadybugDB comes from its Python wheel (`ladybug==0.21.0`, matched to the FTS build; [docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)), so there is no
native build step. Full-text search is a separate native extension: `uv run
oxide prepare` (part of `mise run bootstrap`) downloads this platform's pinned
0.21.0 build ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)) over HTTPS and checks its SHA-256 into
`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/oxide/ladybug-extensions-0.21.0/` (override with
`OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION`). It is the only network access OXIDE makes. The
engine re-verifies the digest before every `LOAD EXTENSION` by path, never
`INSTALL`; without the file the lexical channel reports `unavailable` and
structural retrieval and routing continue. No vector extension exists.

## Frozen baselines

`docs/phase-3/baseline-v1/` (Rust retrieval and routing) is a read-only
oracle: `tests/python/test_baseline.py` asserts the Python engine reproduces
it exactly. A pin or version bump that changes it is a new baseline
directory with a recorded comparison, never a regenerated old one.
Earlier Phase 4/5 reports and DecisionBench/JEV harness instructions are in the
[retired runtime tree](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/f79808a/docs), not local
`docs/phase-4/` or `docs/phase-5/` directories. Reproduction requires that tree.

JavaScript/JSX conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_javascript.py`). The bounded
real-repository and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via
`scripts/eval_javascript.py`; protocol and results: `docs/phase-6/javascript-v1/`.

Go conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_go.py`). The bounded real-repository
and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via `scripts/eval_go.py`; protocol and
results: `docs/phase-6/go-v1/`.

Rust conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_rust.py`). The bounded real-repository,

# Evidence and benchmark review rules (v2)

Scope: any PR/commit/report citing a retrieval, routing, packing or eval
result. These rules are about how a *reviewer* should weigh evidence a
change presents, not about the code paths themselves.

---

### EVD-001 — Benchmark claims must state their provenance
**Severity:** MAJOR · **Scope:** any claim of the form "recall improved" /
"routing beats retrieval" / "X is faster now."

**Invariant:** a benchmark claim must say which config produced it: the
frozen baseline (`tests/python/test_baseline.py` against
`docs/phase-6/baseline-vN/`), a ContextBench run
(`tests/python/contextbench.py` / `contextbench_ts.py`), or an ad hoc run;
which corpus and split (dev vs held-out); and the exact reproduction
command. These are not interchangeable. The frozen baseline is the gate;
ad hoc runs cannot replace it.

**What constitutes a violation:** a PR/report claiming a result without
naming the config, corpus, split and command; updating a frozen baseline
without a stated amendment and protocol note; tuning on held-out.

**Evidence required:** the reviewer must be able to locate the exact command
and config in the PR/doc. If missing, that absence is the finding.

**Exceptions:** `mise run verify` (lint/typecheck/tests) passing is a binary
gate, not a provenance claim.

---

### EVD-002 — Incomplete or cancelled runs are not evidence
**Severity:** MAJOR · **Scope:** ContextBench and any long-running eval.

**Invariant:** a run that was killed, timed out, cancelled or only partially
completed must not be cited to support or refute a claim. A partial result
file is missing data, not a smaller-but-valid version of the final result.

**What constitutes a violation:** citing "N of M tasks passed" from an
interrupted run without completing it or explicitly caveating the numbers
as provisional.

**Evidence required:** the run's own completion signal against what was
reported.

**Exceptions:** reading a result file mid-run for a status check is fine;
citing that read as finished is not.

---

### EVD-003 — A passing test is evidence, not automatic proof of coverage
**Severity:** MAJOR · **Scope:** any reviewer or PR claim of the form
"there's a test for this" / "existing tests still pass."

**Invariant:** a passing test supports only the specific invariant its
assertions actually check. Frozen artifacts must not be regenerated to make
a failure pass; a golden that changes without an intended cause is the
alarm.

**What constitutes a violation:** accepting a diff to a load-bearing
invariant because "existing tests still pass" without checking whether any
existing test pins that invariant; regenerating a frozen artifact to hide a
failure.

**Evidence required:** quote the actual assertion being relied on, not the
test name.

**Exceptions:** none.

---

### EVD-004 — Frozen baselines are not regenerated to pass
**Severity:** BLOCKER · **Scope:** `tests/python/test_baseline.py`,
frozen `docs/phase-6/baseline-vN/`.

**Invariant:** retrieval, routing and packing changes are evaluated against
the frozen baselines; never regenerate a frozen artifact to make a failure
pass. Legacy numbers are historical comparators, not v2 gates.

**What constitutes a violation:** editing a frozen baseline or golden to
make a test pass without a stated amendment and protocol review.

**Evidence required:** the diff to the frozen artifact and the amendment
note.
# Documentation

## Current guidance

- [SPEC](spec/SPEC.md): architecture authority; [BOOTSTRAP](BOOTSTRAP.md): phases and exit gates.
- [ADRs](adr/): decisions and proposals; a Proposed ADR is not an accepted requirement.
- [Public API](public-api.md), [parser limits and language support](parser-limits.md), [platforms](platforms.md).
- [Development workflow](agents/workflow.md) and [review policy](review/README.md).

## Evidence, not current instructions

[Phase 6 research and frozen baselines](phase-6/README.md) separates decision summaries from reproduction inputs and raw results. [Migration audit](migration-audit/README.md) covers the Python rewrite; its [infrastructure summary](migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) explains retained legacy tooling.

Historical reports describe the engine and dependencies at their recorded revision, not necessarily today's product. Old v1 code is pinned at `ac985b28`; the replaced Rust/Bun v2 runtime at `f79808a`. Use the matching tree for reproduction.

Generated standalone architecture viewers were removed as duplicate documentation, not benchmark evidence. The [Rust/SQLite diagram and source](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/architecture) and [Python architecture viewer](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/oxide-architecture.html) remain recoverable. Use SPEC for current architecture rather than maintaining a second generated contract.
# OXIDE review policy (v2)

For a reviewer (Codex, Claude, or human) looking at a diff against this repo.
Generic Python/style feedback is not the point — Ruff and mypy `--strict` already
gate that (`docs/agents/workflow.md`). This policy exists because OXIDE v2 has
invariants a competent reviewer cannot reliably infer from the diff alone:
one-owner storage, published generations, deterministic core policy over a
pinned read view, a vectorless retrieval/routing/packing pipeline, and a
stable typed public API. Read the relevant file below before reviewing a
change in that area.

OXIDE v2 is one Python package (`oxide`, ADR-0011): `oxide.api`/`oxide.models`
are the public boundary; `oxide.core` holds pure repository intelligence and
policy (no database or filesystem access); `oxide.capture` and
`oxide.storage` own worktree capture and LadybugDB; the CLI and `oxide mcp`
are clients of the public API only. Architecture authority is
`docs/spec/SPEC.md` and `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`. When they disagree with this
file, they win.

## Rule files

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `api-surface.md` | Public API stability, integration boundaries, MCP/CLI as clients only, JSON/output contracts |
| `storage-and-generations.md` | LadybugDB ownership, locks, published generations, capture identity, damage classification |
| `core-and-retrieval.md` | Pure core, read view, retrieval/routing/packing, budgets, deterministic ordering, FTS availability |
| `capture-and-language.md` | Worktree capture, symlinks/special files, language extraction, coverage diagnostics |
| `evidence-and-benchmarks.md` | Benchmark provenance, frozen baselines, incomplete runs, what a passing test proves |

## Load-bearing invariants

The v2 invariants live in `docs/spec/SPEC.md` ("Core invariants", "Engine
resources and ownership", "Failure contract") and `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`. Read those
directly rather than relying on this policy's summary; duplicating them risks
drift. Treat every entry there as **BLOCKER** severity under this policy.

## Severity

- **BLOCKER** — silently wrong behavior: data/index corruption, a violated
  load-bearing invariant, a regression in a benchmark-gated property, or
  unconsented network/model-download activity.
- **MAJOR** — a real functional or contract regression that isn't silently
  catastrophic: unbounded traversal, an integration reimplementing repository
  intelligence, a benchmark claim with no reproducible provenance.
- **MINOR** — a real deviation from stated design intent with limited blast
  radius.
- **NIT** — cosmetic drift that doesn't change behavior.

## Reporting a finding

- Point to concrete code: file, and line or function name.
- State the realistic failure path — what input or sequence of operations
  actually reaches the bug.
- Name the violated rule (its stable ID) or invariant.
- Gather the "evidence required" listed under the rule before reporting it.
  A rule you can't find the required evidence for is a question to ask, not
  a finding to file.
- A possibility that isn't tied to a concrete reachable path is speculation.
  Ask it as a question in the review; don't file it as a bug.
# OXIDE review policy

Reviewer-facing invariants for OXIDE v2. Full policy and rule files live in
`docs/review/`; this file is the entry point and is symlinked from there.

- `docs/review/README.md` — policy, severity, reporting.
- `docs/review/api-surface.md` — public API, integrations, output contracts.
- `docs/review/storage-and-generations.md` — store ownership, generations, capture.
- `docs/review/core-and-retrieval.md` — pure core, retrieval/routing/packing, budgets.
- `docs/review/capture-and-language.md` — capture, parsing, language support, identity.
- `docs/review/evidence-and-benchmarks.md` — benchmark provenance and frozen baselines.

Architecture authority: `docs/spec/SPEC.md` and `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`. When they
disagree with this policy, they win.

# OXIDE development workflow

Commands and verification for OXIDE v2, loaded on demand from the root
`AGENTS.md` routing table. Older docs and code comments that cite
"`AGENTS.md`" for a command or harness detail mean this file.

## Commands

[Mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html) is the one entrypoint;
`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).

```bash
mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/
mise run test          #   pytest (tests/python/)
```

`uv run pyrefly check` is an optional second type checker (`[tool.pyrefly]` in
`pyproject.toml`). It is not part of `verify` or CI; mypy `--strict` stays the gate.
On 2026-10-31 it reported 32 errors.

Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/`.
`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
frozen `docs/phase-6/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); v1's README is the
protocol (splits, gate rules, how to freeze a new version) and each later README states
its amendments. Gold is audited (`gold-audit.json`); only verified gold is gated.
Develop on the dev split; never tune on held-out.
`tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` is the same ruler for TypeScript (protocol in
`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, corpora amendment in `typescript-v2/`, latest frozen
baseline `typescript-v15/`; corpora in `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench-ts/corpora-v2/`, and the
sources-only `corpora/` only reproduces v1). Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate
needs ~2 GB of corpora and ~15 minutes, so it is `mise run contextbench-ts`, not part of
`verify`. Run it under the limits below before and after any TypeScript retrieval,
resolution, routing or packing change.
Dependencies live in `pyproject.toml` with a committed `uv.lock`; add them
with `uv add`, never by hand-editing the lock. Keep heavy local runs within
`CPUQuota=200%`/`MemoryMax=3G` (`systemd-run --user --scope`).
To verify another supported Python, set `UV_PYTHON` and a separate
`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` for the entire check. `uv sync --python` alone does not
carry that interpreter choice into a later `uv run`.

OXIDE's engine, CLI, MCP server and distribution need no Node.js, Bun or Rust
toolchain. Native Python dependencies are installed as wheels; the Platforms
workflow enforces wheel-only third-party installation and runs the installed
smoke with only the environment's scripts on `PATH`. That smoke also checks
that MCP advertises exactly `oxide_search`. Optional agent tooling (CodeGraph,
Context7, archify, external MCP servers) and GitHub Actions have their own runtimes;
they are not OXIDE dependencies. See the
[legacy infrastructure audit](../migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) for
the inventory and process ancestry.

Tests never write to real user data: `tests/python/conftest.py` gives every
test a private `OXIDE_DATA_DIR` and XDG locations, fails the session if the
real data location changes, and every subprocess receives explicit private
locations (`env()` and `python()` there; `env()` refuses any location outside
the temporary root). Native probes that could crash, and crash injection, run
only in such subprocesses. Lexical tests need the pinned FTS extension
(`uv run oxide prepare`, once), and the context-quality gate the corpora
(`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py fetch`, once; both are in bootstrap).

## Commits

Commit only when asked. OXIDE v2 work commits on `rewrite/v2` (or a branch
from it, merged back by PR); never commit v2 work to `main`, which keeps the
legacy v1 implementation until the rewrite is merged by explicit decision. Messages use a
lowercase prefix plus an imperative summary: `fix:`, `feat:`, `refactor:`,
`docs:`, `harden:`, `bench:`, `tierb:`.

## Historical reproduction

Retained `eval-agent/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`, `scripts/perf.sh` and Rust
regression/conformance fixtures are historical evidence, not current build steps.
Use the matching pinned tree (`ac985b28` for v1, `f79808a` for the replaced
Rust/Bun v2 runtime), its manifests and original report commands. The legacy
ContextBench evaluator requires Python 3.11; old TS/TSX task verification uses Bun.
See the [infrastructure decision summary](../migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md)
for the retention boundary and pinned original audit. Do not apply v1 CLI,
embedding or SQLite contracts to the Python engine.

## LadybugDB FTS extension

LadybugDB comes from its Python wheel (`ladybug==0.21.0`, matched to the FTS build; [docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)), so there is no
native build step. Full-text search is a separate native extension: `uv run
oxide prepare` (part of `mise run bootstrap`) downloads this platform's pinned
0.21.0 build ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)) over HTTPS and checks its SHA-256 into
`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/oxide/ladybug-extensions-0.21.0/` (override with
`OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION`). It is the only network access OXIDE makes. The
engine re-verifies the digest before every `LOAD EXTENSION` by path, never
`INSTALL`; without the file the lexical channel reports `unavailable` and
structural retrieval and routing continue. No vector extension exists.

## Frozen baselines

`docs/phase-3/baseline-v1/` (Rust retrieval and routing) is a read-only
oracle: `tests/python/test_baseline.py` asserts the Python engine reproduces
it exactly. A pin or version bump that changes it is a new baseline
directory with a recorded comparison, never a regenerated old one.
Earlier Phase 4/5 reports and DecisionBench/JEV harness instructions are in the
[retired runtime tree](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/f79808a/docs), not local
`docs/phase-4/` or `docs/phase-5/` directories. Reproduction requires that tree.

JavaScript/JSX conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_javascript.py`). The bounded
real-repository and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via
`scripts/eval_javascript.py`; protocol and results: `docs/phase-6/javascript-v1/`.

Go conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_go.py`). The bounded real-repository
and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via `scripts/eval_go.py`; protocol and
results: `docs/phase-6/go-v1/`.

Rust conformance runs in `mise run verify` (`test_rust.py`). The bounded real-repository,
oracle and ContextBench diagnostic is reproducible via `scripts/eval_rust.py`; protocol and
results: `docs/phase-6/rust-v1/`.

| CandidateGraph ↔ capsule | Stable bounded encoding, truncation/missingness, no DB internals or hidden labels |
| Capsule ↔ DecisionProvider | Candidate/region/schema/digest correlation, invalid-value rejection, uncertainty/abstention/failure fallback; JEV optional/narrow, no policy or correctness reasoning; training/runtime parity |
| Plan/expansion ↔ bundle | Coherent prerequisites, cycle/fanout limits, source deduplication, strict declared budget, stable ordering/omission reasons |

## Baselines and promotion

Keep lexical-only entry-point retrieval, optional semantic-only, frozen RRF, exact-vector control, deterministic bounded TreeRouter, heuristic/no-model judgments, greedy inclusion, no-expansion packing, and an external no-OXIDE downstream-agent control where appropriate. Use no-routing similarity as a diagnostic ablation only; removing learned judges never removes foundational routing. Freeze manifests, not just aggregate tables.

Report entry-point retrieval, structural routing, context quality, and downstream success separately. Preserve scorer changes and artifact limitations. Historic Qwen3, Arctic, Laya, Julia, JEV, CodeGraph, and ch5 findings apply to their pins and gates; they are neither universal bans nor proof that the new architecture will work. JEV's typed-evidence validity failure left quality gates unread; require fresh validity/calibration/cost evidence before promotion.

Before promoting an experiment, state the information/decision/metric hypothesis and preregister paired quality/cost gates, held-out split, uncertainty method, and rollback to baseline. Do not retrofit gates after seeing test results.

## Follow-up decisions and handoff

Proposed ADR candidates are 0002 (LadybugDB), 0003 (layer/service boundary), 0004 (CandidateCapsule), 0005 (judgments and deterministic policy), 0006 (rebuildable state/no legacy migration), 0007 (TreeIndex / TreeRouter architecture), 0008 (model runner / embedding provider boundary), and 0009 (DecisionProvider and optional JEV integration, complementing policy/calibration in 0005). Identity, transport, token accounting, and concrete inclusion algorithms may need additional focused ADRs. SPEC.md lists the questions and the phase where each must be resolved. None of these candidates is automatically Accepted.

At the end of every future implementation phase, leave: changed scope/boundaries, tests and exact validation evidence, frozen benchmark manifests, unresolved questions/blocked capabilities, and the next authorized phase. Read the full diff for accidental source/dependency/generated-file changes. Do not commit, push, release, change ADR status, or begin unrelated follow-up work without authorization.
- Separate expansion-value targets from relevance to the current entity; useful neighbors need their own evidence and annotation.
- Dataset collection and source-containing traces are opt-in, with repository permissions and retention controls. Do not generate labels or train a model during bootstrap merely to exercise the interface.

This spec constrains data architecture; it does not choose a teacher, training stack, exact label schema, or full collection pipeline.

## Evaluation

**Entry-point retrieval quality != routing quality != context quality != downstream agent success.** Evaluate each stage against its own question and report the denominator and completeness of gold.

| Stage | Metrics | Required controls and cautions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ingestion/knowledge | Entity/edge conformance, resolved/ambiguous coverage, full/incremental logical parity | Malformed/deep source, overloads, duplicate names, same-line attribution, deletes/renames; no silent symbol loss |
| TreeIndex | Region membership/projection fidelity, coverage, scoped navigation, cross-edge preservation, build/update cost | Snapshot-consistent fake/real navigation and malformed/ambiguous structure; no mandatory tree-schema choice |
| Entry-point retrieval | Recall@K, MRR, gold entry-point coverage, channel contribution/entry-point loss | Lexical-only, structural-seed ablation, frozen Phase 3 baseline; same snapshot/candidate limits |
| TreeRouter | Routed required-entity/region coverage, pruning loss, explored regions/nodes/edges, judgment calls, latency | Deterministic bounded traversal, heuristic judge, root/scope fallback, lexical-unavailable mode; no-routing similarity as diagnostic ablation only |
| Capsule | Size, truncation/missingness, runtime/training rendering parity, provenance fidelity | Deterministic fixture capsules; no model-side truncation; length/feature ablations |
| Decision | Precision, recall, AUROC, Brier score, ECE, risk-coverage, accuracy at coverage, repeatability | Heuristic/no-model, optional JEV/local/stronger-judge ablations, retrieval-order baseline, random/order-permutation controls; branch/candidate targets and calibration/test partitions separate |
| Selection/expansion | Required-symbol recall, context noise ratio, structural coherence, evidence loss by stage | Greedy baseline, no expansion, no learned decisions, bounded oracle where gold permits; fixed budgets |
| Packing | Actual canonical token count, budget violations, duplicate-source ratio, prerequisite completeness | Small/zero budgets, oversized items, interval overlap, payload overhead; truncation/coherence diagnostics |
| System | Downstream task success, latency distributions, peak memory, context size, indexing cost/disk size | Fixed agent/model/tools/task snapshots, native agent/no-OXIDE control, cold/warm and offline modes |

Definitions:

- Candidate coverage is gold entities reachable in a named recorded universe: retrieved entry points, routed pool, or expanded pool. Routed coverage sets an inclusion-policy ceiling; entry-point coverage alone does not. Separate entry-point, routing/pruning, selection, expansion, and packing loss. Historical “route loss” terminology may mean retrieval-channel loss and must not be silently reinterpreted as TreeRouter pruning. Report unsupported/missing gold separately.
- Required-symbol recall is annotated required symbols with sufficient evidence in the packed bundle divided by annotated required symbols. A signature-only view may not satisfy a body-required label.
- Noise ratio uses irrelevant context tokens / labeled context tokens. Report annotation coverage; incomplete gold does not make every non-gold token irrelevant.
- Structural coherence can measure satisfied policy-declared prerequisites / all prerequisites and dangling source references. Report trivial empty-bundle behavior separately; it is not proof of task usefulness.
- Decision AUROC and calibration target a declared label/head. Report pooled and within-task behavior where applicable; high global AUROC can hide poor task-local choices.

Evaluation artifacts MUST pin repository revisions/source manifests, source-to-gold mappings, algorithm/configuration versions, model/checkpoint/quantization, scorer version, tokenizer, hardware/runtime, task splits, expected/completed counts, and raw stage results. Preserve correction history when scorer bugs are fixed. Never mix old scorer numbers with newly corrected values as one ruler.

Compare challengers with paired tasks and uncertainty estimates appropriate to repository/worktree clustering. Preregister quality/cost gates before held-out evaluation. A Pareto claim must account for useful evidence, noise, tokens, latency, memory, and indexing cost; more recall or fuller budgets alone do not establish improvement. Hardware-specific historical timings are not universal v2 SLOs.

Simple baselines remain callable, measurable, and frozen by manifest. The historical fixture gate is a regression floor, not proof of broad generalization. Port benchmark intent and data with an explicit compatibility adapter; do not port old architecture to make a harness executable. An unmodified legacy binary at a pinned revision may serve as an external historical comparator.

The workflow docs now say implementation comes first, and about 19 MB of obsolete experiment files are removed and staged. Nothing is committed. `mise run verify` passed: 436 passed, 7 skipped. The 7 skips are the opt-in TypeScript gate.

**The rule now (`AGENTS.md`, with the same wording in `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md` and `docs/agents/workflow.md`)**
- **Normal work:** read the code, change it, add or adjust a test, run `mise run verify`. Features, fixes, language work and refactors need no study, preregistration or report.
- **When an experiment is still needed:** only for claims a test can't settle. That means a change in retrieval, routing or packing quality (the ContextBench gates), a performance claim (`scripts/bench.py` before and after), or promoting an optional judge. You set the pass/fail rule before looking at held-out results, then record the verdict as one line in `docs/phase-6/README.md`. A full report is only needed if a gate, test or code comment will point to it.
- **`docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`:** the preregistration requirement now covers experiments only. The end-of-phase handoff checklist is replaced by "the PR description is the handoff".
- **`docs/agents/workflow.md`:** has a new "Default loop" section. The separate paragraphs for each language are now one general rule, and I dropped an outdated count of pyrefly errors.
- **`docs/review/evidence-and-benchmarks.md`:** EVD-001 and EVD-004 had wrong baseline paths, now fixed. Changes that make no quality or performance claim are exempt from needing benchmark evidence.

**Evidence cleanup (`docs/phase-6`, 41 MB → 22 MB)**
- **Deleted:** 10 closed studies that nothing references (agc-v2, change-classification, entry-retrieval-diagnostic, file-localization, java-v1-opencode, leann-graph-storage, outline-comparison, routed-module-selection, router-reachability, source-body-retrieval). Each verdict stays as one line in the phase-6 decision map.
- **Trimmed:** the old baselines (baseline-v3, v5–v17 and typescript-v3–v14) keep only their README with the protocol changes; their result JSON files are gone.
- **Kept:** everything a gate, test, CI job, code comment or ADR cites. That includes baseline-v1, v2, v4 and v18, typescript-v1, v2 and v15, the language milestone folders, release-blockers and fts-footprint.
- **Links:** links that pointed at the deleted folders now point to a pinned copy of the full tree at `eb43ac1`.

**Research:** I checked agents.md and GitHub's review of 2,500 AGENTS.md files. Both say to keep it to commands, boundaries and stack details, and to keep it short. `AGENTS.md` grew by only one line.

**Not changed:**
- SPEC § Evaluation (the "preregister quality/cost gates" line) is the architecture authority and only covers experiments, so I left it alone.
- The long Phase 6 changelog in BOOTSTRAP is still there; trimming it was out of scope.
- I didn't run the TypeScript ContextBench gate (it's opt-in and takes about 15 minutes), though `typescript-v15` was kept untouched.

**Risk:** the working tree also has changes I didn't make, in `src/oxide/{api.py,core/navigation.py,storage/*}`, `scripts/smoke_dist.py`, two test files and `docs/phase-6/fts-footprint/README.md`. The [Rust/SQLite diagram and source](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/architecture) and [Python architecture viewer](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/oxide-architecture.html) remain recoverable. Use SPEC for current architecture rather than maintaining a second generated contract.
# Research decisions and benchmark evidence

Start with [current documentation](../README.md), not historical reports. These studies record decisions at their pinned revisions; they do not change SPEC, public API contracts or ADR status. Current gate commands and baseline selection live in [workflow](../agents/workflow.md).

## Retention

- Kept: what a gate, test, script or source comment reads (`baseline-v1`, `-v2`, `-v4`, `-v18`; `typescript-v1`, `-v2`, `-v15`; language milestones; `fts-footprint`, `indexing-throughput`, `output-integrity`, `release-blockers`), and studies behind a shipped behavior or an ADR. Never regenerate them to make a failure pass.
- Superseded `baseline-v*` / `typescript-v*` keep only their README (the protocol amendment chain); their results are reproducible from the pinned commit in that README.
- Closed studies with no current consumer were removed; their verdicts are in the table below. Everything, including removed directories and raw results, is at [this immutable evidence tree](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/phase-6) under the same relative path.
- Historical harnesses run at their pinned revision, not against the current checkout.

## Decision map

| Question | Reports |
|---|---|
| Graph ranking, dispatch and candidate-pool ceilings | [v1](graph-v1/README.md), [v2](graph-v2/README.md), [v3](graph-v3/README.md) |
| Graph navigation completeness and targeted resolution | [initial audit](graph-navigation/README.md), [correction and follow-up](graph-navigation-v2/README.md), [NetworkX projection](networkx-v1/README.md) |
| Agent-guided context and where to stop | [AGC](agc/README.md), v2 REJECT (adoption; removed), [v3](agc-v3/README.md), [v4](agc-v4/README.md) |
| Optional judges and deterministic decision boundary | [seam](decision-seam/README.md), [study v1](decision-study-v1/README.md), [v2](decision-study-v2/README.md), [v3](decision-study-v3/README.md), [reliability](jev-reliability/README.md) |
| Historical JEV ordering milestones | [M1](jev-order-m1/README.md), [M2](jev-order-m2/README.md), [M3 release readiness](jev-order-m3/README.md), [release blockers](release-blockers/README.md) |
| Storage, graph caches and FTS footprint | LEANN/storage: REJECT compaction, DEFER traversal memo (removed); [FTS corrections and optimizations](fts-footprint/README.md) |
| Output serialization | [TOON rejection](toon-serialization/README.md) |
| Retrieval diagnostics | [path hints](path-hint-utility/README.md) (PROMOTE). Removed, all closed: source bodies REJECT, entry-retrieval taxonomy (diagnostic), file localization NOT VIABLE, router reachability NEGATIVE, routed selection INCONCLUSIVE |
| Structure and output experiments | [ast-grep feasibility](astgrep-feasibility/README.md), outlines REJECT (removed), [output integrity](output-integrity/README.md), [structural MCP trial](structural-mcp-trial/README.md) |
| Capture/indexing performance | [throughput](indexing-throughput/README.md), [incremental indexing](incremental-indexing/README.md), change classification NOT WORTH IT (removed) |

## Language milestone evidence

[JavaScript](javascript-v1/README.md), [Rust](rust-v1/README.md), [Go](go-v1/README.md), [Java](java-v1/README.md), [C](c-v1/README.md), [C++](cpp-v1/README.md). TypeScript evidence is the versioned protocol series above. Current support boundaries are documented under [parser limits](../parser-limits.md), not inferred from an old milestone's claims.

# Bootstrapping the OXIDE architectural rewrite

## Purpose and authority

This is guidance for future Codex/Claude implementation sessions. **This documentation session must not implement, scaffold, or refactor the rewrite.** OXIDE v2 names an architectural generation, not a SemVer release or a requirement to ship v0.2 first.

OXIDE is an open-source context engine for agents. OXIDE indexes repository knowledge into a structural TreeIndex and routes each task through that structure to construct a bounded, high-value ContextBundle for software agents. Its mission remains: **OXIDE transforms repository structure into task-specific context.** Agents consume context; OXIDE remains agent-agnostic and is not an autonomous coding agent.

Use the foundational flow: repository → TreeIndex → query → TreeRouter (lexical/vector entry points) → CandidateGraph / CandidateCapsules → DecisionProvider → deterministic Rust policy → structural expansion → ContextPacker → ContextBundle. Routing may also request bounded branch-value judgments through DecisionProvider. Do not postpone TreeIndex/TreeRouter until after similarity retrieval or model adoption.

Before implementing, read [SPEC.md](spec/SPEC.md), all **Accepted** ADRs, root `AGENTS.md`, and applicable scoped instructions. Also read [ADR-0001](adr/0001-oxide-v2-rewrite.md), which is currently **Proposed**. Read any other Proposed ADR relevant to the work, but do not treat it as Accepted or change its status automatically.

The user’s rewrite instruction and SPEC.md supersede legacy maintenance assumptions about preserving SQLite, IDs, APIs, and module layout. Other repository working rules still apply, including documentation evidence, scope discipline, and no unrequested commits/pushes/releases. Resolve conflicts between SPEC.md and an Accepted ADR in writing before dependent implementation.

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

1. Work on the separate rewrite branch `rewrite/v2` when implementation is authorized. Inspect branch and working-tree state first; protect existing work. Do not broadly refactor main.
2. Existing main is historical evidence, not an architecture template. Do not port modules/code by default. Reuse requires a stated spec requirement, a boundary-fit explanation, and appropriate tests.
3. Do not preserve legacy SQLite schemas, row IDs, migrations, cache locations, or accidental public APIs. New derived state uses an isolated namespace and is rebuildable from captured source.
4. When spec and old code disagree, follow the spec. When the spec is ambiguous, record the ambiguity, affected phase, alternatives, and proposed decision. Continue independent work; do not invent a permanent ID/schema/transport/model policy to unblock scaffolding.
5. Keep semantic embeddings, JEV, and all learned judges optional. Preserve deterministic lexical entry points, structural TreeRouter exploration, heuristic DecisionProvider and ContextPacker with no runner/model/network requirement.
6. Models judge; deterministic Rust decides. Rust owns thresholds, traversal, routing/stopping, expansion, inclusion, budget, fallback, and final packing. Never overwrite retrieval scores with logits/probabilities from another score space. JEV judges relevance/value/branch/neighbor usefulness and uncertainty, not code correctness.
7. Put TreeIndex/TreeRouter and repository intelligence in the kernel; put OXIDE I/O/resources/provider request orchestration in runtime; put integrations/presentation in TS. TS must not become a second router, selector, or source parser.
8. Do not expose LadybugDB objects, native IDs, result rows, or Cypher through kernel, capsule, or TS service contracts. Implement the kernel-owned KnowledgeStore contract in runtime infrastructure.
9. Start as a modular monolith. Logical kernel/runtime separation is mandatory; many tiny crates/packages are not. Justify each new compilation, reuse, runtime, or API boundary.
10. Add meaningful tests at every architectural boundary and stage. Test declared invariants, degraded states, cancellation/publication, and limits rather than mirroring implementation details.
11. Maintain frozen measurable baselines, raw stage artifacts, and provenance. Do not regenerate gold or erase negative results to make a challenger pass.
12. For every feature, state what information it adds, which decision it improves, and which metric should move. Require evidence before promotion to defaults.
13. Inspect current official technology documentation at the pinned release. Documentation capability claims are not proof that the Rust adapter builds, loads extensions, or handles mutations safely.
14. Do not execute repository code/build hooks as part of context indexing. Respect repository scope and source privacy at hydration, expansion, model, trace, and export boundaries.
15. Structure before similarity. Retrieval finds entry points; routing finds context. TreeIndex retains graph cross-edges; do not force all repository relationships into a single-parent tree. Specify a minimal structural projection/navigation contract without prematurely freezing its physical schema or routing algorithm.
16. Design DecisionProvider support from the beginning for heuristic, optional JEV, future local specialized, and optional stronger judges. Keep subject correlation, uncertainty/abstention, request limits and deterministic fallback in the initial contracts; no live JEV is required for CI/bootstrap.
17. OXIDE owns context engineering, not model serving. External runners execute inference. Prefer Ollama and llama.cpp embedding adapter boundaries; Sentence Transformers is research/reference infrastructure, and native inference is a future benchmark-driven exception.
18. Discovery is advisory. Unconfigured semantics remains unavailable with lexical/structural operation and optional setup choices. Persist configured provider/model identity; never switch because another runner appears. Validate explicit reconfiguration and invalidate incompatible vectors. Do not install weights or start inference serving as an automatic discovery side effect.

### Amendment 2026-10-15: Python engine (ADR-0011)

Rules 5–9, 13 and 16–18 were written for the Rust/TypeScript stack and a planned vector channel. They keep their text above as the record; from Phase 6 they read:

- **5.** Keep JEV and every learned judge optional. There are no embeddings or vectors. Preserve deterministic lexical entry points, structural TreeRouter exploration, the heuristic value and ContextPacker with no model or network requirement.
- **6.** Models judge; deterministic code decides: thresholds, traversal, stopping, inclusion, budget, fallback and packing.
- **7.** Repository intelligence lives in `oxide.core`; I/O in `oxide.capture` and `oxide.storage`; integrations (CLI, `oxide mcp`, future editors) are Python clients of `oxide.api` and never parse, route or select.
- **8.** LadybugDB objects, native IDs, rows and Cypher stay inside `oxide.storage`; `oxide.models` and the API expose domain values only.
- **9.** One package with clear modules. A new package or dependency needs a demonstrated reuse, packaging or API reason.
- **13.** Documentation claims are not proof that the Python binding builds, loads extensions or behaves at the pin; verify (ADR-0011 § Storage verification).
- **16.** A `DecisionProvider` seam returns only as a scoped follow-up behind `oxide.core.packing.value`, with subject correlation, abstention and deterministic fallback; no live judge in CI.
- **17–18.** Obsolete: no embedding runners, discovery or vector invalidation.
- **19 (new).** Native libraries do recursive and latency-sensitive work (tree-sitter queries, LadybugDB queries, hashing); Python holds bounded policy over small sets.

## Before Phase 0

Record the requested scope, branch/base revision, applicable instructions, and unresolved decisions from SPEC.md. Confirm later implementation is actually authorized; this document itself is not a request to start coding.

Create an evidence inventory referencing the inspected historical main revision `ac985b28fcff7663aedadf2db5b40aa2dc325580` or a newly inspected pin. Preserve fixture/language/relation tests, embedding identity/staleness/recovery cases, ContextBench scorer fixes, evaluation scripts/raw artifacts, performance harnesses, and rejected experiments. Check whether artifacts are committed, machine-local, or dependent on retired experimental code. Preserve references; do not copy the entire old source tree into a new skeleton.

Historical targets include `fixtures/benchmark.json`, `fixtures/py_repo`, `fixtures/ts_repo`, language/relation conformance data, `eval-agent/benchmark/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`, `scripts/perf.sh`, and the evidence reports listed in SPEC.md. Legacy test code may embed old IDs/CLI/schema assumptions; port its semantic assertions rather than its storage/API coupling.

## Bootstrap phases and exit gates

The phases are an initial dependency order, not immutable project management. A change of order needs a short rationale, updated dependencies, and unchanged correctness gates. TreeIndex/TreeRouter, DecisionProvider (including JEV capability planning), and embedding-provider contracts begin in Phase 1 with evaluation, trace, uncertainty/fallback and fixture artifacts. The complete deterministic path precedes learned promotion; do not defer foundational routing/provider design to Phase 5.

### Phase 0 — Minimal workspace and boundaries

Deliver:

- A minimal Rust workspace/host with kernel and runtime responsibilities separated in dependencies and tests.
- A TS workspace for the control-plane boundary, without importing legacy integrations wholesale.
- A documented minimal versioned request/result/error contract and resource-owner lifecycle. Choose a minimal local test transport explicitly; do not silently freeze daemon or native-addon architecture.
- A dependency map placing TreeIndex, TreeRouter and ContextPacker in the kernel, provider clients/orchestration in runtime, and inference execution outside OXIDE. No model-serving stack or native model dependency is scaffolded.
- Pinned toolchains/dependency lockfiles, Mise tasks, and CI for formatting/linting, Rust tests, TS type checks/tests, boundary checks, and cross-language contract tests.

Exit gate:

- A typed request reaches a Rust stub/domain operation and returns a validated result/error without TS domain logic or kernel integration imports.
- Build/test tasks are reproducible and CI matches Mise commands. No network or model is required for kernel tests.
- Package/crate choices and unresolved transport/ownership issues are documented.

### Phase 1 — Domain contracts and fake store

Deliver:

- Repository/snapshot/derivation and domain ID types, entities, relations, source references, query context, structural regions, entry-point/routed candidate/plan/bundle concepts, and typed errors.
- A documented ID/namespace policy covering overloads, nesting, duplicate names, byte-range attribution, case/path rules, and collision handling before relying on identity in ingestion.
- KnowledgeStore read/write/publication/capability contracts and a fake/in-memory store.
- TreeIndex projection/navigation and TreeRouter input/output/trace/limit contracts, preserving graph cross-edges and partial coverage. Start with a minimal documented test hierarchy; physical schema and advanced routing remain open.
- An initial typed DecisionProvider and bounded candidate/region capsule contract with deterministic heuristic/fake providers, confidence/abstention, subject/version correlation, and fallback. Identify JEV candidate/branch/neighbor judgment capabilities now; no code-correctness reasoner or live API dependency.
- Embedding-provider identity/capability/batching/error contracts with fake runner fixtures; plan Ollama/llama.cpp adapters, advisory discovery, persisted identity and explicit reconfiguration.
- Contract tests and deterministic manifests/fixtures for scoped lookup, adjacency bounds, completeness, incompatible derivations, and publication visibility.

Exit gate:

- Kernel operations run against the fake store with no database/model/integration.
- IDs and lookup scope are unambiguous and no DB-native type enters the domain.
- Failed/unpublished generations cannot appear as valid current snapshots; capabilities and missingness are explicit.
- Minimal TreeIndex navigation and TreeRouter/DecisionProvider boundary fixtures run offline, with cycles/cross-edges, missing/uncertain judgments and declared traversal limits. JEV/provider capabilities do not leak vendor types or define Rust policy.
- Unconfigured semantics, unavailable configured runner, and newly discovered alternative runner have distinct states; none triggers a silent model/provider switch.

### Phase 2 — LadybugDB adapter and ingestion

Deliver:

- A pinned LadybugDB/Rust adapter feasibility record: native build/target packaging, offline build, extension linking/loading, persistence/reopen, concurrency/ownership, cancellation, and mutation/rebuild observations.
- A physical graph schema mapped to domain identity/provenance and TreeIndex navigation through KnowledgeStore. Resolve node/facet representation for tests and ambiguous/unresolved references without treating the tree projection as all graph knowledge.
- Runtime source capture/scope enforcement and repository/file/symbol-to-TreeIndex ingestion for an explicitly chosen language slice, with conservative relation extraction and coverage diagnostics.
- Atomic publication and safe discard/recovery of incomplete generations; a separately scoped derived-store location.

Exit gate:

- Fake and real stores pass the common contract suite for supported operations.
- TreeIndex membership/navigation and cross-edges agree with the published entity/source snapshot; a request cannot mix projections/generations.
- Restart/rebuild, deletes, partial source, duplicate names/overloads, same-line nesting, and failed publication preserve intended logical knowledge.
- One runtime owns read/write DB resources; a second client cannot open an unsafe independent owner. Supported concurrency is documented with tests at the pinned API.
- Unknown vector/FTS update or Rust extension behavior remains a blocked capability, never an assumed success.

Start with full rebuild if necessary. Add incremental indexing later with full/incremental parity before advertising it; do not import migrations to accelerate this phase.

### Phase 3 — Entry-point retrieval, TreeRouter and evaluation baseline

Deliver:

- Deterministic lexical and structural-seed retrieval that returns an entry-point CandidateSet; optional vector retrieval with explicit embedding-space identity through external Ollama/llama.cpp adapters.
- A deterministic bounded TreeRouter baseline over TreeIndex, including root/scope fallback, heuristic branch judgments through the Phase 1 contract, visited sets/stopping limits, minimal routed candidates/capsules and route traces. Refine schemas explicitly; advanced algorithms remain optional experiments.
- Provider configuration/health/readiness and bounded local discovery, batch/identity compatibility and deadline behavior. External runners execute inference; detection never enables semantics or changes persisted configuration by itself.
- A stage evaluation harness, gold-to-domain mapping, corrected scorer provenance, cold/warm indexing/query measurements, entry-point channel/fusion dumps and routing coverage/pruning/cost traces.
- Frozen lexical-only entry-point and weighted-RRF controls plus deterministic structural-routing controls; optional semantic-only and exact-vector controls. A no-routing similarity path is an evaluation ablation, not normal architecture. Treat historical K=60 / 0.6–0.4 as a comparison configuration, not a v2 default requirement.
- Tested explicit fallback for unavailable/invalid/incompatible semantic evidence.

Exit gate:

- Retrieval finds entry points; TreeRouter constructs the structural candidate universe. Neither returns final packed context or hides channel failures.
- Snapshot filters precede candidate limits; score/rank semantics, ordering, cutoffs, and hydration identity are reproducible.
- Recall@K, MRR, entry-point coverage, routed required-entity/region coverage, pruning loss and routing work can be measured separately from inclusion/packing outcomes; ANN quality is compared to exact search when enabled.
- No semantic configuration, missing runner, model-identity drift and additional discovered runner all preserve observable lexical/structural routing and never silently substitute providers. Ollama/llama.cpp adapter tests can use fixtures without executing inference in CI.
- Frozen manifests/raw results survive later experiments. Fixture passing is reported as a regression floor, not generalization proof.

Implement deterministic TreeIndex/TreeRouter and lexical entry points first; vector extensions, JEV and learned inference are not prerequisites for offline context.

### Phase 4 — Routed evidence, optional JEV and deterministic context

Deliver:

- CandidateGraph of routed evidence with bounded nodes/edges/fanout/depth, stable order, TreeIndex/route provenance, cycle handling, and truncation diagnostics.
- Refined versioned CandidateCapsule and region/branch subject semantics plus canonical dataset/inference rendering, evolving the earlier provider contract with explicit size/missingness/truncation rules.
- Heuristic candidate/branch decisions, a simple greedy inclusion baseline, and a SelectionPlan with reasons and coherent evidence groups. TreeRouter exploration and final inclusion remain distinct.
- Optional JEV adapter design/implementation against the existing DecisionProvider contract, with narrow candidate/branch/neighbor value questions, version/response validation, uncertainty, deadlines, request limits, privacy and fake-service fixtures. Live use is opt-in and requires current API/capability verification; support does not imply quality promotion or code-correctness reasoning.
- Bounded structural expansion and kernel ContextPacker with a declared canonical payload/tokenizer, overlap deduplication, view reduction, and omission reporting.

Exit gate:

- End-to-end deterministic offline context uses TreeIndex/TreeRouter/heuristic DecisionProvider/ContextPacker without any learned component, JEV, or inference runner. Optional JEV work does not block the deterministic phase exit.
- Entry-point retrieval, TreeIndex navigation, TreeRouter, graph, capsules, decisions, plan, expansion, and final bundle can be independently inspected/replayed.
- Capsule/dataset rendering agrees; no gold/final policy outcome enters model input.
- Graph membership is distinct from inclusion; expanded neighbors compete within the same budget and terminate under limits.
- Packer handles zero/tiny budgets, oversized entities, overlapping source, and unavailable prerequisites while satisfying the declared token budget and coherence rules.
- Required-symbol recall, labeled context noise, tokens, coherence and cost are measurable against no-expansion/heuristic/greedy controls.
- JEV disabled, failed, malformed, uncalibrated or abstaining leaves bounded heuristic routing/inclusion functional; captured provider responses replay deterministically even if the service itself is nondeterministic.

TreeIndex/TreeRouter are foundational concepts with open schema/algorithm decisions. TreeSelect, if retained as a name for an inclusion experiment, is separate from TreeRouter and remains unspecified until objective, TreeIndex view, prerequisites, complexity, and evaluation are documented. Greedy inclusion plus deterministic bounded routing is sufficient for the baseline; do not implement an unspecified optimizer.

### Phase 5 — Judge specialization, calibration and DecisionBench

Deliver:

- Optional local specialized judge and stronger-judge escalation experiments through the existing DecisionProvider/subject contract. The foundational interface, JEV capability planning and uncertainty/fallback have already been designed in earlier phases.
- Runtime provider-client orchestration and shared routing/candidate request limits, timeouts and explicit privacy/cost rules. External runners own inference execution; native execution needs separate benchmark justification.
- DecisionBench record/provenance/split design aligned to runtime candidate/branch capsules; realistic entry-point/routed/branch hard negatives, teacher uncertainty/audit, visitation-bias controls, and repository-held-out calibration/test procedures. Sentence Transformers may be a research/reference tool.
- Separate branch/candidate evaluation for discrimination, validity/repeatability, calibration, risk-coverage, position bias, fallback/routing, and end-to-end request/runner cost; preserve no-model and heuristic controls. Existing JEV validity failure is not evidence of either quality gain or quality rejection.

Exit gate:

- Disabled, failed, malformed, uncertain, or unavailable learned inference all leave deterministic context construction functional and observable.
- Models cannot alter traversal rules, thresholds, expansion, hard inclusion, budget, or fallback. Judgments remain separate from entry-point scores and TreeRouter/inclusion/packing policy outcomes; no judge is treated as a code-correctness reasoner.
- Dataset records use the same input semantics/renderer as inference, and policy decisions are not mislabeled as ground-truth relevance.
- No learned model is promoted without a frozen repository-held-out quality/calibration/cost protocol. A trained checkpoint is not required to complete this architectural interface phase.

### Phase 6 — Python migration (ADR-0011)

Replace the Rust kernel/runtime and Bun control plane with one Python package, without new retrieval experiments or model training.

Delivered (2026-10-15):

- `oxide` package (`src/oxide/`), uv-managed; `mise run verify` runs Ruff (lint, format), mypy `--strict` and pytest.
- Vertical slice over persisted state: `index_repository` → `search` → `build_context`, typed results, CLI (`oxide index|search|context|prepare`).
- Python language slice with the Rust `oxide-python-v1` semantics, one tree-sitter query; capture with `.gitignore`, skips and consistency retry; LadybugDB generations with lock, atomic publication, read-back and digest-verified hydration.
- Retrieval and TreeRouter reproduce `docs/phase-3/baseline-v1` exactly on all 7 tasks (test oracle). Context reaches Phase 4 config B's required-symbol recall 1.0 at 1,024 units.
- Tests for parsing/indexing, graph relations, retrieval, budgets/provenance, persistence/recovery/ownership, errors, CLI subprocesses and data isolation (every test and subprocess gets a private data location).
- Rust/Bun production code removed; recoverable at `f79808a`.

Exit gates for the migration:

1. Every public operation the Rust/TS stack offered or planned has a Python equivalent or a recorded decision not to port it (ADR-0011 § What was removed).
2. Retrieval and routing reproduce the frozen Phase 3 baseline; context quality is no worse than the Phase 4 heuristic baseline on its fixture.
3. `mise run verify` passes from a clean checkout after `mise run bootstrap` (FTS extension and, since the quality gate, the ContextBench corpora).

Delivered (2026-10-16): `oxide mcp`, a stateless FastMCP server over `oxide.api` (`oxide_search`, `oxide_context`; stdio, and stateless Streamable HTTP on loopback), opening the repository per call and tested with FastMCP's client in memory, over stdio and over HTTP with private data locations (`docs/public-api.md` § MCP).

Delivered (2026-10-16): the context-quality regression gate. `tests/python/contextbench.py` evaluates entry-point recall/MRR, routed coverage, packed recall, utilization and loss diagnostics at 256/1,024/4,096 units on 7 fixture and 37 ContextBench Python tasks (human gold, dev/held-out split by repository); `docs/phase-6/baseline-v1/` freezes the protocol, tasks, per-task results and manifest, and `test_contextbench.py` gates quality and output compatibility separately in `mise run verify`. Read-only MCP and CLI requests no longer create empty stores (`open_repository(..., create=False)`).

Delivered (2026-10-16): ContextBench scorer v2 and gold audit (`docs/phase-6/baseline-v2/`). Every annotated span is checked against its own content at the pinned commit: 176 of 208 verify (2 after a recorded path correction), 32 are reported separately as unverified with their class (annotation range errors, patched-revision content, drift, empty). Gold lines exclude blank lines, module-level gold is coverable through file entities, and every lost span is attributed to entry, routing, unsupported evidence, selection or budget. The engine output is unchanged.

Delivered (2026-10-16): module-level evidence in ContextPacker (`oxide-select-greedy-v3`, `oxide-payload-v3`, `docs/phase-6/baseline-v3/`). A parsed Python file retrieved by lexical match or hint packs its module-level source (imports, constants, top-level statements) as bounded runs between its top-level declarations, with a first-run header view and explicit omissions; files reached only by routing stay containers.

Closed (2026-10-16): the selection R&D iteration. Its last experiment, letting routed-only files pack module-level evidence, was INCONCLUSIVE at the preregistered dev-coverage check (one dev task; [routed-module-selection](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/phase-6/routed-module-selection)); `oxide-select-greedy-v3` stays the default.

Each generation seals the parse facts of its Python files (`facts.json`, digest in the manifest); `index()` reuses them for unchanged bytes while resolution and publication stay whole-snapshot, so the result equals a full rebuild (parity tested over cross-file edits, moves, deletions and damaged facts). On 3,539 files an edit re-index drops from ~14.5 s to ~9.8 s; cold builds cost ~9% more. `IndexReport` names added/modified/deleted paths and parsed/reused counts; `oxide index` prints stage pro

Delivered (2026-10-17): the TypeScript context-quality baseline (`docs/phase-6/typescript-v1/`, `contextbench-ts-v1`). `tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` applies the ContextBench-py ruler to 8 fixture and 81 ContextBench TypeScript tasks (mui, vue held out; vscode, code-server, darkreader dev), with a gold audit (two annotation defects handled: absolute paths, `cat -n` content), grammar-derived module lines validated against OXIDE on 7,353 files, and a structural cause for every span lost before packing (router bound, unresolved import by a path oracle, partial parse, no path). Verified `span_r

Delivered (2026-10-17): large-repository reliability and TypeScript module resolution (`docs/phase-6/typescript-v2/`, `contextbench-ts-v2`). The LadybugDB load pool is `BUFFER_POOL` plus twice the CSV bytes a load copies ([docs/large-repositories.md](large-repositories.md)): all 14 VS Code corpora index with the default settings (v1: 0 of 14), with results identical to v1 and the same peak RSS as the old 512 MiB override. Structural search stays a Python API (`Repository.structural_search`, `oxide[structural]`): a preregistered agent trial (`docs/phase-6/structural-mcp-trial/`, REJECT) found agents with grep already at 0.978 shape-task F1 against 0.994 with structural mode, and they never called the search 

Delivered (2026-10-23): graph intelligence (`docs/phase-6/graph-v1/`). 235	| TS ↔ runtime | Versioned types/errors, request validation, cancellation/lifecycle; no prose parsing or TS selection |
236	| Runtime ↔ kernel | Integration-free domain input/output; resource/provider failures explicit; effective policy stays Rust |
237	| Runtime ↔ external runners | Configured model/provider identity, batch semantics and deadlines; advisory discovery/no automatic switches; semantic-unavailable fallback, no serving ownership |
238	| Kernel ↔ KnowledgeStore | Domain IDs, snapshot-scoped views, bounds, provenance, atomic publication; same fake/real contracts |
239	| Knowledge ↔ TreeIndex ↔ TreeRouter | Snapshot/projection-consistent regions/cross-edges, bounded navigation, entry-point/root fallback, stable traversal/pruning trace; heuristic routing works offline |
240	| Captured source ↔ knowledge | Byte/digest/range fidelity, unsupported/partial parsing, overload/nesting identity; full/incremental convergence when enabled |
241	| CandidateGraph ↔ capsule | Stable bounded encoding, truncation/missingness, no DB internals or hidden labels |
242	| Capsule ↔ DecisionProvider | Candidate/region/schema/digest correlation, invalid-value rejection, uncertainty/abstention/failure fallback; JEV optional/narrow, no policy or correctness reasoning; training/runtime parity |
243	| Plan/expansion ↔ bundle | Coherent prerequisites, cycle/fanout limits, source deduplication, strict declared budget, stable ordering/omission reasons |
244	
245	## Baselines and promotion
246	
247	Keep lexical-only entry-point retrieval, optional semantic-only, frozen RRF, exact-vector control, deterministic bounded TreeRouter, heuristic/no-model judgments, greedy inclusion, no-expansion packing, and an external no-OXIDE downstream-agent control where appropriate. Use no-routing similarity as a diagnostic ablation only; removing learned judges never removes foundational routing. Freeze manifests, not just aggregate tables.
248	
249	Report entry-point retrieval, structural routing, context quality, and downstream success separately. Preserve scorer changes and artifact limitations. Historic Qwen3, Arctic, Laya, Julia, JEV, CodeGraph, and ch5 findings apply to their pins and gates; they are neither universal bans nor proof that the new architecture will work. JEV's typed-evidence validity failure left quality gates unread; require fresh validity/calibration/cost evidence before promotion.
250	
251	This applies to experiments, not to ordinary implementation: features, fixes, language slices and refactors are accepted on tests and `mise run verify` (plus the ContextBench gates when they touch retrieval, routing or packing). Before promoting an experiment that claims a quality or cost improvement, fix its pass/fail gates, held-out split and rollback to baseline in advance. Do not retrofit gates after seeing test results.
252

Identity, transport, token accounting, and concrete inclusion algorithms may need additional focused ADRs. SPEC.md lists the questions and the phase where each must be resolved. # baseline-v18: PR #45 review-fix identity amendment

The review fixes for PR #45 bump versions that feed the frozen identity:
`typescript` `oxide-typescript-v4` (callback and block scopes in TypeScript/TSX) with
`FACTS_FORMAT` `oxide-typescript-facts-v3`, `python` `oxide-python-v7` (re-export
chains bounded at 32), `java` `oxide-java-v2` (inheritance diamonds keep inherited
methods), and `router` `oxide-router-bfs-v3` (store reads bounded by an edge
allowance; a cut layer is deferred with `stopped_by: "edges"`). The derivation id
hashes every component version, so every index's id changes. None of these paths fires
on the pinned corpora.

## Measured against baseline-v17

Same tasks, gold audit, scorer, budgets, corpora and tolerance.

| File | Difference from v17 |
| --- | --- |
| `metrics.json` | byte-identical |
| `results.json` | 88 differences, all `versions.derivation` (`sha256:1b2f…` → `sha256:2f7a…`) and `versions.router` (`bfs-v2` → `bfs-v3`); every task's entries, routed set and payload are identical |
| `manifest.json` | 39 `derivation` ids (38 corpora and `versions`), `versions.router`, `oxide_source`, and the `baseline`/`protocol` labels (set to v18 by hand, as in v17) |

This is an identity amendment, not a quality change. `test_output_is_compatible`
reported only the router and derivation changes before the freeze.

(run once before the `BASELINE` switch, under a 200% CPU / 3 GB cap).
# typescript-v15: PR #45 review fixes (TypeScript callback scopes, bounded routing reads)

Versions: `typescript` `oxide-typescript-v4` and facts `oxide-typescript-facts-v3`
(callback and block bodies are opaque scopes in TypeScript/TSX, as they already were in
JavaScript, so a declaration hidden in a callback can no longer capture an outer call),
`python` `oxide-python-v7`, `java` `oxide-java-v2`, and `router` `oxide-router-bfs-v3`
(store reads bounded by an edge allowance). The derivation id changes for every index.

## Measured against typescript-v14

| File | Difference from v14 |
| --- | --- |
| `metrics.json` | byte-identical (every gated metric, both splits) |
| `results.json` | 89 `versions.derivation`, 89 `versions.router`; 4 tasks' routed sets ([12], [16], [20], [60]) and 9 tasks' `route.deferred`/`fanout_truncations`/omission counts; task [60] now stops by `depth`, not `regions`. No `stopped_by: "edges"` |
| `manifest.json` | 82 corpus `derivation` ids, `versions`, `oxide_source`, and resolution counts in 81 of 82 corpora. The `baseline`/`protocol` labels are fixed strings and unchanged, as in v14 |

Resolution totals over the 82 corpora (measured):

| | v14 | v15 | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| calls resolved | 1,330,762 | 1,191,021 | −139,741 (−10.5%) |
| calls ambiguous | 244,076 | 216,060 | −28,016 |
| calls unresolved | 4,228,486 | 4,396,243 | +167,757 |
| references resolved | 88,753 | 88,665 | −88 |

The lost edges are calls to declarations inside callback or block bodies (for example a
helper declared inside a `describe(() => …)` callback), which are no longer entities'
children and so stay unresolved; calls from callbacks to outer declarations still
resolve (checked on a probe). This is the JavaScript policy applied to TypeScript: it
gives up those local edges so a hidden declaration can never be a false target.
Gated quality is unchanged; the routing differences are inside tolerance.

`performance.json` is re-measured under the 200% CPU / 3 GB cap: `index_s` is
0.74–1.19× v14's (median 0.86×); `max_rss_mb` is 33 MB lower to 53 MB higher. Different
sessions, so a diagnostic only.

Command: `OXIDE_CONTEXTBENCH_TS=1 uv run --locked python tests/python/contextbench_ts.py run --out docs/phase-6/typescript-v15`.
# Phase 6 Python context-quality baseline v4 (`contextbench-py-v4`)

A versioned re-freeze, not an engine-quality change. The TypeScript language slice
([docs/typescript.md](../../typescript.md)) adds two derivation components
(`typescript`, `typescript-parser`), so every generation's `derivation_id` changed,
and the compatibility gate failed as designed (`versions.derivation`). The protocol,
scorer, tasks, gold audit, corpora, splits, budgets, tolerance and gated metrics are
[v3's](../baseline-v3/README.md), and so is every engine version but the derivation.
v1–v3 stay as frozen.

## What changed, measured

- No corpus contains a TypeScript file (`*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.mts`, `*.cts`, counted in
  every pinned checkout), so no entity, relation or lexical document changed.
- Against v3, `results.json` differs only in `versions.derivation` of each task:
  entries, routes and the payload hashes at 256/1,024/4,096 units (`compat`), all
  metrics, loss stages and gold states are identical. `metrics.json` is byte-identical
  to v3's.
- `manifest.json` differs in the corpus `derivation` ids, `oxide_source`, and the
  environment's package list, which now names `tree-sitter-typescript` 0.23.2.
- Two runs gave byte-identical `results.json`, `metrics.json` and `manifest.json`.

Results are therefore v3's tables unchanged.
