# Python rewrite infrastructure: decision summary

Historical audit, 2026-10-21, beginning at `c70786db`; generated-artifact follow-up began at `905102de`. This is infrastructure evidence, not a retrieval experiment or current dependency/version inventory. Current installation requirements are in [platforms](../platforms.md), commands in [workflow](../agents/workflow.md), architecture in [SPEC](../spec/SPEC.md) and [ADR-0011](../adr/0011-python-engine-vectorless.md).

## Decisions

- Keep the Python engine/distribution independent of Node, Bun and Cargo. Native libraries arrive as wheels; CI verifies wheel-only third-party installs and installed-artifact smoke with a restricted PATH. MCP must advertise only `oxide_search`.
- Retain historical semantic fixtures, regression tests, evaluation harnesses and migration parity probes. Their Rust/Bun/Python-3.11 requirements apply to reproducing old results, not current OXIDE installation. `fixtures/ts_repo` is active parser input, not an npm application to install.
- Keep optional agent tooling (CodeGraph, Context7, archify, external MCPs) and GitHub Actions distinct from product dependencies. Measured Node process ancestry belonged to agent hosts/tools; this was a bounded process snapshot, not continuous tracing or proof about arbitrary plugins.
- Remove stale Rust/TypeScript agent instructions and strengthen packaging checks. Preserve user edits, research worktrees and tracked historical npm fixtures.
- Follow-up removed only ignored root `target/` and `node_modules/`, after separate authorization, descriptor/path checks and bounded process inspection. No source, dependency, baseline, public export or derivation version changed.

## Measurements and verification limits

Reported Linux x86_64 checks: canonical Ruff/strict mypy/pytest passed (265 passed, seven opt-in TS cases skipped); separate frozen TS gate 17 passed (~942 s in follow-up), under two-core/3 GB limits. Wheel/sdist installed smokes passed on Python 3.12.15, 3.13.16 and 3.14.8, including single-tool MCP, indexing/edit/reopen and locking. Original unrelated tracked diff remained byte-identical. Hosted Windows/macOS execution and a fresh FTS download were not verified locally.

Removed entries represented 2,236,022,784 bytes (`target/`) plus 168,534,016 bytes (`node_modules/`) of allocated blocks. Observed free-space increase was **1,025,773,568 bytes**, not the summed allocation: npm files had surviving hard links, and Btrfs sharing/compression and concurrent activity affect accounting. No claim of reclaiming all directory allocation is justified.

## Provenance and historical access

The [full original audit](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) records inventories, exact test receipts, process ancestry and limitations. Raw receipts were temporary/external (`/tmp/oxide-infra-audit/`, `/tmp/oxide-generated-cleanup/` and associated runners/logs); they were not committed, so this summary is not a self-contained rerun bundle. Retained [migration benchmarks and parity probes](README.md) have separate provenance.

Legacy v1 invariants (SQLite, persisted symbol IDs, embedding-space compatibility, bounded hydration, atomic publication) are [pinned historical reference](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/eb43ac1070d8724d31a0be49bc7357c7132fb90f/docs/agents/invariants.md), **not v2 requirements**. Original v1 code is pinned at `ac985b28fcff7663aedadf2db5b40aa2dc325580`; the replaced Rust/Bun v2 tree is recoverable at `f79808a`. Reproduce historical claims in those trees; port semantic lessons only where current SPEC requires them.
# Python migration audit: fixes and evidence (2026-10-15)

This pass follows up the audit of the Python engine (ADR-0011) on `rewrite/v2`.
The `M`/`L` IDs are that audit's labels. Every claim below is marked
**measured** (a test or probe ran) or **inferred**.

## Fixed and regression-tested

| ID | Defect | Fix | Regression |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | A damaged `graph.lbug` (random bytes, truncated) raised raw `RuntimeError` from every call and was never rebuilt. A malformed `MANIFEST.json` raised `KeyError`, and a corrupt `repo.json` raised `JSONDecodeError` | `View` validates the manifest's shape before any native call. It maps native open and read failures (`RuntimeError`, measured as the only class raised) to `StoreCorrupt` and closes what it opened. It also compares the stored entity count with the manifest, because an empty file opens as an empty database (measured). `index()` rebuilds; `repo.json` damage fails closed at open and is never rewritten | `test_recovery.py` (damage runs in a subprocess), `test_cli.py::test_a_damaged_store_is_a_stable_error_then_rebuilt` |
| M2 | A `Repository` dropped without `close()` held its lock until the process exited | `weakref.finalize(store, os.close, fd)` holds only the descriptor, never the store; `close()` runs it once | `test_lifecycle.py` (GC releases the lock to another process, no descriptor leak over 30 cycles, exception paths, idempotent close) |
| L1 | A crash between the two renames of a same-name rebuild left `CURRENT` dangling and needed manual deletion | `_recover` moves `<g>.replaced` back when `<g>` is absent, and `index()` then rebuilds. A failure in that window (not a crash) is undone in place. Any other dangling `CURRENT` still fails closed, and nothing is deleted | `test_a_crash_between_the_rebuild_renames_is_undone_on_open` (child killed with `os._exit` at the second rename) |
| L2 | A deleted retained source file was reported `unchanged` forever | `is_current` verifies every retained source file's existence and digest | `test_missing_retained_source_is_never_reported_unchanged` |
| L3 | `--limit -5` and `--budget -1` crashed with tracebacks and exit 1 | `InvalidArgument` (`invalid_argument`, also a `ValueError`) validates limit, budget, query, hints and selection before any query is built, with bounds `MAX_LIMIT = 1000` and `MAX_BUDGET = 2**20` | `test_retrieval.py::test_malformed_arguments_*`, `test_cli.py::test_expected_errors_never_print_a_traceback` |
| L4 | A data directory inside the repository indexed itself and never reached `unchanged` | Capture excludes the data directory and its `repos/` by `(st_dev, st_ino)`, so nested paths and symlink aliases are excluded too, with no string-prefix matching | `test_capture.py::test_a_data_location_inside_the_repository_is_never_captured` (`state`, `deep/nested/state`, a symlink alias) |
| L5 | Store and extension paths containing `'` or `\` were refused, undocumented | Escaped instead (`\` → `\\`, `'` → `\'`). The probe below shows byte-exact round trips. Only paths that are not UTF-8 are refused (`invalid_path`) | `test_native.py::test_paths_with_quotes_and_backslashes_work_end_to_end` (the FTS extension itself loaded from a quoted path) |
| Unverified concern | The derivation version check ran after the native database was opened | The component comparison moved into `View`, before the open | `test_derivation_compatibility_is_checked_before_the_database_opens` (a garbage `graph.lbug` under a foreign `ladybug` component gives `incompatible_index`, not `store_corrupt`) |

Run against the pre-fix source, 17 of the 23 `test_recovery.py` cases fail and
all 23 pass after the fix (measured). The 6 that pass on both lock in behavior
that was already correct: a non-JSON manifest, a foreign `root`, garbage
`CURRENT` text, and crashes before and after `CURRENT` moves.

### Correction: an OXIDE mirror of the release builds (prepared, not published)

The maintainer chose the mirror on 2026-10-24. Upstream restoring its files would still
help other users. The issue is drafted in [ladybug-issue.md](ladybug-issue.md), not posted.

- **What it is.** One release, `ladybug-fts-0.21.0` on `Kiy-K/oxide`. It holds the four
  files from run 36488319988, unmodified and renamed
  `libfts-0.21.0-<platform>.lbug_extension`. It also carries `SHA256SUMS` and
  `NOTICE.txt`, and its body is [fts-mirror/RELEASE.md](fts-mirror/RELEASE.md). The
  notices are LadybugDB core and extensions (MIT), plus what the FTS extension links:
  Snowball (BSD-3-Clause), RE2 (BSD-3-Clause), cppjieba and limonp (MIT). Each was read
  at the pinned commits `d7225cea54` and `bf74ab654a`.
- **What changed in OXIDE.** Only the URL in `ladybug._fts_build`. `FTS_BUILDS`, the
  digest checks, `OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION` and the error messages are unchanged. There is no
  fallback host, and no path skips the digest.
- **Immutability.** The pins are the guarantee: a replaced or tampered asset fails
  `oxide prepare`, as upstream's did. GitHub immutable releases add to that. Assets
  can't be changed after publishing, and the tag can't be moved or reused. The repo
  setting is off today (`{"enabled":false}`), and turning it on affects every later
  release of this repo.
- **Checked locally (Linux x86-64).**
  - The staged files match all four pins, and the four artifact zips match
    GitHub's recorded digests.
  - `prepare_fts` was run cold against a local server holding the staged mirror. It
    accepted the file, and the full suite passed with it (381 passed, 7 skipped).
  - Served under the same name, the incompatible upstream build was refused ("does not
    match"), and no file was written.
  - `LOAD EXTENSION` loads the mirrored file into `ladybug==0.21.0`. The upstream
    replacement fails with the undefined symbol.
- **Not yet checked:** the real download from GitHub, and cold installs on macOS and
  Windows. Both need the release to be published and pushed (below).

#### Publication steps (each needs the maintainer's authorization)

Run them in this order. Pushing first would make `oxide prepare` 404 on every platform.

```sh
M=~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/fts-provenance/mirror   # the staged, verified files
cp docs/phase-6/release-blockers/fts-mirror/{NOTICE.txt,SHA256SUMS} "$M"/
(cd "$M" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)
# 1. Optional, repo-wide: make new releases immutable.
gh api -X PUT -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10" repos/Kiy-K/oxide/immutable-releases
# 2. Create it as a draft with every asset attached, then publish it. The tag targets a pushed commit.
gh release create ladybug-fts-0.21.0 -R Kiy-K/oxide --draft --latest=false --target 0121d80453644f4542f66178d67598c8c15c80a8 \
  --title "LadybugDB FTS extension 0.21.0 (mirror)" \
  --notes-file docs/phase-6/release-blockers/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md \
  "$M"/libfts-0.21.0-*.lbug_extension "$M"/SHA256SUMS "$M"/NOTICE.txt
gh release edit ladybug-fts-0.21.0 -R Kiy-K/oxide --draft=false
# 3. Check what GitHub serves, then fetch it cold through the real code path.
D=$(mktemp -d ~/Projects/oxide-eval-data/fts-provenance/served.XXXX)
gh release download ladybug-fts-0.21.0 -R Kiy-K/oxide -D "$D" && (cd "$D" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)
env -u OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION XDG_CACHE_HOME="$D/cache" uv run oxide prepare
# 4. Push rewrite/v2. CI and Platforms then fetch the asset cold on all four platforms.
only as `v0.21.0` (there is no 0.21.1 or 0.21.2 build, checked 2026-10-18), and its
compiled-in version table ends at 0.21.0. ladybug 0.21.2's ends at 0.21.1. Linux and
macOS ran that mismatched pair cleanly. On Windows an FTS query crashed the process
with an access violation, after a second generation was published in the same process
(Platforms run 39104738648). That is the patch-level ABI mismatch upstream has seen
before (LadybugDB/ladybug#971). So the ladybug pin is 0.21.0, whose version table
matches the extension. Both ContextBench gates gave identical entries, routes,
payloads and metrics on 0.21.0 (`baseline-v7`, `typescript-v4`). Move the pin forward
together with a matching FTS build.

## FTS extension pins

`oxide prepare` downloads the platform's build of the LadybugDB FTS extension 0.21.0
from the OXIDE release `ladybug-fts-0.21.0`
(`github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/releases/download/ladybug-fts-0.21.0/libfts-0.21.0-<platform>.lbug_extension`).
It checks the download against the SHA-256 pinned in `oxide.storage.fts.FTS_BUILDS`, and the
engine checks it again before every load. The release holds LadybugDB's own builds,
unmodified, with LadybugDB's license and third-party notices
([fts-mirror/](phase-6/release-blockers/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md)). The digests were taken
on 2026-10-17 (file types: ELF x86-64, Mach-O x86_64, Mach-O arm64, PE32+ x86-64). On a
platform without a pin, `fts_unavailable` names the platform, and `oxide prepare` fails
with the same message without touching the network. Search and context still run with
the lexical channel `unavailable`. That is a supported degraded mode, not a failure.

**Provenance (verified 2026-10-24):** all four pinned files are byte-identical to the
artifacts of upstream CI run 36488319988, built at `d7225cea54`, the `v0.21.0` tag that
`ladybug==0.21.0` is built from. OXIDE mirrors them because upstream's
`extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.21.0/` is not immutable. Since 2026-10-20 it has served a
build of upstream main at `225bc28088` (core 0.22.0-dev) for Linux x86-64, macOS x86-64
and Windows. That build fails to load into core 0.21.0 (undefined symbol, measured on
Linux). To move the pin forward, mirror the new version's release builds the same way,
after checking that they load into the matching core. See
[docs/phase-6/release-blockers/](phase-6/release-blockers/README.md).

CI fetches the FTS build cold on every run, so a missing or replaced asset fails CI
instead of hiding behind a cache.

# baseline-v18: PR #45 review-fix identity amendment

The review fixes for PR #45 bump versions that feed the frozen identity:
`typescript` `oxide-typescript-v4` (callback and block scopes in TypeScript/TSX) with
`FACTS_FORMAT` `oxide-typescript-facts-v3`, `python` `oxide-python-v7` (re-export
chains bounded at 32), `java` `oxide-java-v2` (inheritance diamonds keep inherited
methods), and `router` `oxide-router-bfs-v3` (store reads bounded by an edge
allowance; a cut layer is deferred with `stopped_by: "edges"`). The derivation id
hashes every component version, so every index's id changes. None of these paths fires
on the pinned corpora.

## Measured against baseline-v17

Same tasks, gold audit, scorer, budgets, corpora and tolerance.

| File | Difference from v17 |
| --- | --- |
| `metrics.json` | byte-identical |
| `results.json` | 88 differences, all `versions.derivation` (`sha256:1b2f…` → `sha256:2f7a…`) and `versions.router` (`bfs-v2` → `bfs-v3`); every task's entries, routed set and payload are identical |
| `manifest.json` | 39 `derivation` ids (38 corpora and `versions`), `versions.router`, `oxide_source`, and the `baseline`/`protocol` labels (set to v18 by hand, as in v17) |

This is an identity amendment, not a quality change. `test_output_is_compatible`
reported only the router and derivation changes before the freeze.

> Correction pointer (2026-10-16): superseded as the gate by
> [`baseline-v2`](../baseline-v2/README.md), which audits the gold and corrects the
> scorer (blank lines, module-level gold, loss stages) on the same engine output. The
> numbers below are v1's and stay as frozen.

The frozen quality baseline of the Python engine (ADR-0011) and the regression gate
that `mise run verify` runs against it. It is independent of the historical Rust
artifacts in `docs/phase-3/baseline-v1` and `docs/phase-4/baseline-v1`, which stay
untouched and keep their own exact-reproduction test (`tests/python/test_baseline.py`).

Claims: entry-point retrieval, TreeRouter coverage and packed-context quality of the
deterministic offline engine on 44 tasks with independently defined gold. It makes no
downstream-agent claim, and the 7-task fixture split is a regression floor, not a
generalization result (SPEC § Evaluation).

## Protocol (written before any real-repository result was produced)

Everything in this section was fixed before the harness first ran on the ContextBench
tasks. Changing it later needs a new baseline version, never an edit here.

### Tasks and gold

- **fixture** (7 tasks, dev): every Python query of `fixtures/benchmark.json` and
  `fixtures/structural_benchmark.json`, corpus `fixtures/py_repo`. The query is the
  task `text`; a structural task's `anchor_symbol` is passed as a symbol hint, as in
  Phase 3. Gold symbols (`file#A.b`) map to line spans with Python's own `ast` (the
  `def`/`class` line through `end_lineno`), never with OXIDE's parser or results.
- **ContextBench** (37 tasks): `EuniAI/ContextBench` `data/full.parquet` (sha256
  `2f56535bdc73eb8a68bf4ebb49789d8e9cd4f219ea60df6290b85278aee61ca8`), every
  `language == python` task whose repository has at most 250 tracked `*.py` files at
  every one of its base commits (a cost rule, measured from git trees without running
  OXIDE): psf/requests (6), pallets/flask (1), mwaskom/seaborn (1), pydata/xarray (17),
  pytest-dev/pytest (12). The query is the `problem_statement`, verbatim, without hints.
  Gold is the human-annotated `gold_context` line spans (1-based, inclusive). Each span
  stores the sha256 of its whitespace-normalized `content`; a span whose corpus lines
  do not match is reported as unverified, never dropped.
- Corpus: the tracked `*.py` files of the repository at `base_commit` (`git archive`),
  indexed whole. Non-Python files are left out, a declared difference from a full
  checkout.
- **Splits, by repository** (SPEC § Training-data implications): **dev** = fixture,
  requests, flask, seaborn (15 tasks); **heldout** = xarray, pytest (29 tasks), the two
  eligible repositories with the most tasks. Retrieval, routing or packing work is
  developed and inspected on dev. Held-out per-task results are recorded for the gate,
  but are not used to choose or tune a change; read them only to evaluate a finished
  change.

### Metrics

Overlap: an entity covers a gold span when they share a line of the same file. Only
symbols count for span metrics (a file entity would cover everything).

- `entry_recall@k` (k = 1, 5, 20): gold spans covered by a symbol among the first k
  `search` entries (seeds first, then lexical rank; default limit 20) / gold spans.
- `entry_mrr`: 1 / position of the first entry covering any gold span, 0 if none.
- `entry_file_recall`: gold files containing any entry (any category) / gold files.
- `routed_coverage`: gold spans covered by a TreeRouter candidate symbol (the
  inclusion ceiling) / gold spans.
- For each budget B in 256, 1024, 4096 `oxide-units-v1`:
  - `span_recall@B`: gold spans whose every line lies in packed items / gold spans;
  - `line_recall@B`: gold lines inside packed items / gold lines (distinct lines);
  - `file_recall@B`: gold files with a packed item / gold files;
  - `utilization@B`: used / budget (a diagnostic; filling the budget is not a goal);
  - `gold_unit_share@B`: units of items overlapping gold / used (labeled precision;
    incomplete gold makes the rest unlabeled, not irrelevant).
- Per gold span and budget: `complete`, `partial` or `missed`, with the stage that
  lost it (`entry`, `routing`, or the packer's omission reasons, or `graph-limit`).
- Diagnostics per bundle: items, header-only entities, omissions by stage and reason,
  degradations, route bounds (regions, deferred, fanout truncations, stop reason).

Aggregates are macro means over the tasks of a split.

### Gate rules (`tests/python/test_contextbench.py`)

1. **Quality.** For each split, every gated metric (`entry_recall@5`, `entry_recall@20`,
   `entry_mrr`, `routed_coverage`, `span_recall@B` and `line_recall@B` for every budget)
   must stay at or above its frozen value minus **0.02** absolute. The engine is
   deterministic, so there is no sampling noise to absorb; the tolerance only lets
   small line-level drift pass. Losing one span on the smallest split moves its mean
   by more than 0.02. Improvements pass.
2. **Invariants.** Every bundle has `used <= budget`, building it twice gives the same
   bundle, and no task fails. Corpus identities (commit and digest of the `*.py` tree)
   must equal the manifest; a changed corpus is reported as such, not as a quality change.
3. **Output compatibility, separately.** Per task, the entry order, the routed

# Bootstrapping the OXIDE architectural rewrite

## Purpose and authority

This is guidance for future Codex/Claude implementation sessions. **This documentation session must not implement, scaffold, or refactor the rewrite.** OXIDE v2 names an architectural generation, not a SemVer release or a requirement to ship v0.2 first.

OXIDE is an open-source context engine for agents. OXIDE indexes repository knowledge into a structural TreeIndex and routes each task through that structure to construct a bounded, high-value ContextBundle for software agents. Its mission remains: **OXIDE transforms repository structure into task-specific context.** Agents consume context; OXIDE remains agent-agnostic and is not an autonomous coding agent.

Use the foundational flow: repository → TreeIndex → query → TreeRouter (lexical/vector entry points) → CandidateGraph / CandidateCapsules → DecisionProvider → deterministic Rust policy → structural expansion → ContextPacker → ContextBundle. Routing may also request bounded branch-value judgments through DecisionProvider. Do not postpone TreeIndex/TreeRouter until after similarity retrieval or model adoption.

Before implementing, read [SPEC.md](spec/SPEC.md), all **Accepted** ADRs, root `AGENTS.md`, and applicable scoped instructions. Also read [ADR-0001](adr/0001-oxide-v2-rewrite.md), which is currently **Proposed**. Read any other Proposed ADR relevant to the work, but do not treat it as Accepted or change its status automatically.

The user’s rewrite instruction and SPEC.md supersede legacy maintenance assumptions about preserving SQLite, IDs, APIs, and module layout. Other repository working rules still apply, including documentation evidence, scope discipline, and no unrequested commits/pushes/releases. Resolve conflicts between SPEC.md and an Accepted ADR in writing before dependent implementation.

## Non-negotiable implementation rules

1. Work on the separate rewrite branch `rewrite/v2` when implementation is authorized. Inspect branch and working-tree state first; protect existing work. Do not broadly refactor main.
2. Existing main is historical evidence, not an architecture template. Do not port modules/code by default. Reuse requires a stated spec requirement, a boundary-fit explanation, and appropriate tests.
3. Do not preserve legacy SQLite schemas, row IDs, migrations, cache locations, or accidental public APIs. New derived state uses an isolated namespace and is rebuildable from captured source.
4. When spec and old code disagree, follow the spec. When the spec is ambiguous, record the ambiguity, affected phase, alternatives, and proposed decision. Continue independent work; do not invent a permanent ID/schema/transport/model policy to unblock scaffolding.
5. Keep semantic embeddings, JEV, and all learned judges optional. Preserve deterministic lexical entry points, structural TreeRouter exploration, heuristic DecisionProvider and ContextPacker with no runner/model/network requirement.
6. Models judge; deterministic Rust decides. Rust owns thresholds, traversal, routing/stopping, expansion, inclusion, budget, fallback, and final packing. Never overwrite retrieval scores with logits/probabilities from another score space. JEV judges relevance/value/branch/neighbor usefulness and uncertainty, not code correctness.
7. Put TreeIndex/TreeRouter and repository intelligence in the kernel; put OXIDE I/O/resources/provider request orchestration in runtime; put integrations/presentation in TS. TS must not become a second router, selector, or source parser.
8. Do not expose LadybugDB objects, native IDs, result rows, or Cypher through kernel, capsule, or TS service contracts. Implement the kernel-owned KnowledgeStore contract in runtime infrastructure.
9. Start as a modular monolith. Logical kernel/runtime separation is mandatory; many tiny crates/packages are not. Justify each new compilation, reuse, runtime, or API boundary.
10. Add meaningful tests at every architectural boundary and stage. Test declared invariants, degraded states, cancellation/publication, and limits rather than mirroring implementation details.
11. Maintain frozen measurable baselines, raw stage artifacts, and provenance. Do not regenerate gold or erase negative results to make a challenger pass.
12. For every feature, state what information it adds, which decision it improves, and which metric should move. Require evidence before promotion to defaults.
13. Inspect current official technology documentation at the pinned release. Documentation capability claims are not proof that the Rust adapter builds, loads extensions, or handles mutations safely.
14. Do not execute repository code/build hooks as part of context indexing. Respect repository scope and source privacy at hydration, expansion, model, trace, and export boundaries.
15. Structure before similarity. Retrieval finds entry points; routing finds context. TreeIndex retains graph cross-edges; do not force all repository relationships into a single-parent tree. Specify a minimal structural projection/navigation contract without prematurely freezing its physical schema or routing algorithm.
16. Design DecisionProvider support from the beginning for heuristic, optional JEV, future local specialized, and optional stronger judges. Keep subject correlation, uncertainty/abstention, request limits and deterministic fallback in the initial contracts; no live JEV is required for CI/bootstrap.
17. OXIDE owns context engineering, not model serving. External runners execute inference. Prefer Ollama and llama.cpp embedding adapter boundaries; Sentence Transformers is research/reference infrastructure, and native inference is a future benchmark-driven exception.
18. Discovery is advisory. Unconfigured semantics remains unavailable with lexical/structural operation and optional setup choices. Persist configured provider/model identity; never switch because another runner appears. Validate explicit reconfiguration and invalidate incompatible vectors. Do not install weights or start inference serving as an automatic discovery side effect.

### Amendment 2026-10-15: Python engine (ADR-0011)

Rules 5–9, 13 and 16–18 were written for the Rust/TypeScript stack and a planned vector channel. They keep their text above as the record; from Phase 6 they read:

- **5.** Keep JEV and every learned judge optional. There are no embeddings or vectors. Preserve deterministic lexical entry points, structural TreeRouter exploration, the heuristic value and ContextPacker with no model or network requirement.
- **6.** Models judge; deterministic code decides: thresholds, traversal, stopping, inclusion, budget, fallback and packing.
- **7.** Repository intelligence lives in `oxide.core`; I/O in `oxide.capture` and `oxide.storage`; integrations (CLI, `oxide mcp`, future editors) are Python clients of `oxide.api` and never parse, route or select.
- **8.** LadybugDB objects, native IDs, rows and Cypher stay inside `oxide.storage`; `oxide.models` and the API expose domain values only.
- **9.** One package with clear modules. A new package or dependency needs a demonstrated reuse, packaging or API reason.
- **13.** Documentation claims are not proof that the Python binding builds, loads extensions or behaves at the pin; verify (ADR-0011 § Storage verification).
- **16.** A `DecisionProvider` seam returns only as a scoped follow-up behind `oxide.core.packing.value`, with subject correlation, abstention and deterministic fallback; no live judge in CI.
- **17–18.** Obsolete: no embedding runners, discovery or vector invalidation.
- **19 (new).** Native libraries do recursive and latency-sensitive work (tree-sitter queries, LadybugDB queries, hashing); Python holds bounded policy over small sets.

## Before Phase 0

Record the requested scope, branch/base revision, applicable instructions, and unresolved decisions from SPEC.md. Confirm later implementation is actually authorized; this document itself is not a request to start coding.

Create an evidence inventory referencing the inspected historical main revision `ac985b28fcff7663aedadf2db5b40aa2dc325580` or a newly inspected pin. Preserve fixture/language/relation tests, embedding identity/staleness/recovery cases, ContextBench scorer fixes, evaluation scripts/raw artifacts, performance harnesses, and rejected experiments. Check whether artifacts are committed, machine-local, or dependent on retired experimental code. Preserve references; do not copy the entire old source tree into a new skeleton.

Historical targets include `fixtures/benchmark.json`, `fixtures/py_repo`, `fixtures/ts_repo`, language/relation conformance data, `eval-agent/benchmark/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`, `scripts/perf.sh`, and the evidence reports listed in SPEC.md. Legacy test code may embed old IDs/CLI/schema assumptions; port its semantic assertions rather than its storage/API coupling.

## Bootstrap phases and exit gates

The phases are an initial dependency order, not immutable project management. A change of order needs a short rationale, updated dependencies, and unchanged correctness gates. TreeIndex/TreeRouter, DecisionProvider (including JEV capability planning), and embedding-provider contracts begin in Phase 1 with evaluation, trace, uncertainty/fallback and fixture artifacts. The complete deterministic path precedes learned promotion; do not defer foundational routing/provider design to Phase 5.

# Decisions

The standing rules, delivered state, settled research verdicts and evaluation protocol of
OXIDE v2, in one place. It replaces `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md` and the Phase 6 decision map.
[SPEC](spec/SPEC.md) is the architecture authority and the [ADRs](adr/) record individual
decisions. This file never changes an ADR's status, and a Proposed ADR is not a requirement.

The reports, harnesses and raw results behind every verdict below are frozen at
[`013e791`](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs)
(`docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`, `docs/phase-6/<study>/`, `docs/migration-audit/`). Historical
harnesses run at that pin, not against the current checkout. The v1 implementation is
pinned at `ac985b28`, and the replaced Rust/Bun v2 runtime at `f79808a`.

# OXIDE architectural specification

## Status and authority

- Status: **Draft architectural source of truth for the proposed rewrite**.
- Architectural generation: **OXIDE v2**. This is not a SemVer release designation and implies no dependency on reaching v0.2.
- Date: 2026-10-07.
- Top-level decision: [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-oxide-v2-rewrite.md), **Proposed**.
- Implementation decision: [ADR-0011](../adr/0011-python-engine-vectorless.md), **Accepted** 2026-10-15: one Python process, LadybugDB through its Python wheel, vectorless retrieval. It supersedes ADR-0003 and the Rust/TypeScript and vector/embedding parts of ADR-0001.
- Future implementation instructions: [BOOTSTRAP.md](../BOOTSTRAP.md).

**Amended 2026-10-15 (ADR-0011).** OXIDE v2 is implemented in Python. Read "core" (the `oxide.core` modules: pure repository-intelligence policy) where older text said Rust kernel, "engine" (the `oxide` package: API, capture, storage) where it said Rust runtime, and "integrations" (Python clients of the public API: the CLI, the `oxide mcp` server, future editor adapters) where it said TypeScript control plane. Vector and embedding retrieval is removed from the architecture, not deferred. Sections below were edited accordingly; where historical Rust phases are cited, they are evidence, recoverable at commit `f79808a`.
[ADR-0002](../adr/0002-ladybugdb-knowledge-store.md) and [ADR-0010](../adr/0010-domain-identity-and-source-capture.md) are Accepted; [ADR-0011](../adr/0011-python-engine-vectorless.md) (Accepted) moved the implementation to Python and removed vectors. Additional ADRs for transport, inclusion algorithm, or token accounting may be warranted once concrete alternatives are evaluated. The eight entries above are candidates, not existing Accepted ADRs; ADR-0001 only establishes the top-level rewrite and product direction.

## Milestones

Use the dependency order and exit gates in [BOOTSTRAP.md](../BOOTSTRAP.md):

1. **Phase 0:** Minimal workspace, logical kernel/runtime separation, TS workspace, Mise and CI; specify the minimal typed boundary.
2. **Phase 1:** Domain identities/snapshots, TreeIndex/TreeRouter navigation contracts, KnowledgeStore/fake store, initial DecisionProvider/heuristic and embedding-provider contracts including JEV capability planning, conformance fixtures.
3. **Phase 2:** LadybugDB feasibility/adapter/schema, source capture and repository/file/symbol-to-TreeIndex ingestion; atomic publication and coverage diagnostics.
4. **Phase 3:** Lexical entry points, deterministic TreeRouter baseline with minimal bounded region/candidate judgments, optional Ollama/llama.cpp vector adapters, evaluation harness and frozen retrieval/routing baselines.
5. **Phase 4:** Refined CandidateGraph/capsules, optional JEV adapter against the existing contract, deterministic inclusion policy, bounded expansion, ContextPacker and coherent budget validation. JEV remains opt-in and is not required to exit the phase.
6. **Phase 5:** Local specialized/stronger-judge experiments, calibration and selective routing, DecisionBench collection/evaluation. Confidence/abstention and the provider interface already exist in the earlier phases; a trained model is not required for architecture acceptance.
7. **Phase 6 — Python migration (ADR-0011):** the Python engine replaces the Rust/Bun implementation, starting with the `index_repository → search → build_context` slice; see BOOTSTRAP § Phase 6.

Start structural and provider contracts, uncertainty/fallback tests, evaluation and trace fixtures in Phase 1; do not defer TreeIndex/TreeRouter or DecisionProvider design to Phase 5. Grow canonical capsule schemas through explicit versions as routing/candidate data becomes concrete. Implement the deterministic lexical/structural routing/context path before treating ANN, JEV or learned inference as prerequisites. Incremental/full parity and multi-client concurrency can be staged, but are required before those capabilities are advertised. Dependencies may justify moving a phase; document the change and retain exit gates.

## Acceptance criteria for bootstrap

- `docs/review/capture-and-language.md` — capture, parsing, language support, identity.
- `docs/review/evidence-and-benchmarks.md` — benchmark provenance and frozen baselines.

## When to activate

Use OXIDE when the task needs **discovery**: you don't yet know which files
are relevant. Skip it entirely when:

- the exact file/location is already known (from a stack trace, a prior
  search, or the user telling you),
- the task is a tiny, isolated edit,
- you need an exact literal string match (use grep/ripgrep instead),
- OXIDE already returned weak/empty evidence for this task — fall back to
  normal repository exploration rather than retrying rephrased queries.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# OXIDE perf harness: measures cold index, no-change reindex, single-file edit,
# search/context latency, peak RSS, and DB size on a deterministic synthetic repo.
# Usage: scripts/perf.sh [modules_per_lang]
set -euo pipefail

# Argument is either a module count (synthetic repo, the default) or a path to
# an existing repository, which is copied to $WORK and measured in place. The
# copy matters: these runs write a .oxide/ index and edit one file, and doing
# that to a real checkout in situ would be rude.
N="${1:-200}"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
BIN="$ROOT/target/release/oxide"
OFFLINE_EMBEDDER=(env -u OXIDE_EMBED_URL -u OXIDE_EMBED_MODEL OXIDE_EMBED_NATIVE=hashed)
WORK="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/oxide-perf-$$"
